errorCodes.meaning: The submitted `name` does not match a known hosting domain. See [category conventions](../../../_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md#2-unknown-domain-error).
`state: disabled` was requested for the system default domain; the default must first be moved elsewhere via `domain/set-default`.
`state: active` was requested for a domain already purged after its grace period expired; it can no longer be re-activated and must be recreated via `domain/create`.

defaultDomain.description: When `true`, this domain is the host's default — new DIDs created without an explicit domain are hosted here. Exactly one entry SHOULD carry `defaultDomain: true`.

name.description: Hosting domain name (e.g. `did.example.com`). Compared case-insensitively; producers SHOULD emit lowercase canonical form.

purgeAt.description: Earliest RFC3339 timestamp at which the host's background sweep is allowed to purge content for a disabled domain. Operators with administrative authority MAY override the wait via `domain/purge`.

status.description: Domain lifecycle state. A `disabled` domain still serves existing DIDs in read-only mode for the host's configured grace period before purge becomes eligible.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

name.description: The hosting domain whose state is being set.

state.description: Desired domain state. `active`: the domain is in active service and accepts new DID registrations (re-activating a disabled domain cancels any pending purge). `disabled`: existing DIDs remain readable for the host's grace period, but no new DIDs may be hosted under it. Declarative — requesting the state the domain is already in is an idempotent no-op.
